evidence.observation: get_parser builds a configargparse.ArgumentParser with auto_env_var_prefix='AIDER_', config_file_parser_class=configargparse.YAMLConfigFileParser and default_config_files. These are the two non-CLI input sources: environment variables (AIDER_*) and YAML config files become the parser's defaults, while tokens given in argv are parsed afterwards by argparse, which is what makes explicit CLI input overridable-but-winning.

The tri-state fixture itself: group.add_argument('--analytics', action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=None, help='... (default: random)'). default=None is the 'unset/ask' state, True forces analytics on, False forces it off, and BooleanOptionalAction auto-registers the explicit negative spelling --no-analytics that the contract exercises.

The unrelated two-state options used as the 'defaults must not move' witnesses: --auto-commits (BooleanOptionalAction, default=True) and --dirty-commits (BooleanOptionalAction, default=True). Overriding --analytics from the CLI must leave these at True, exactly as tests/basic/test_main.py::test_main_args checks for its own CLI flips.

The pre-existing, already-fixtured option is a different one: --show-diffs is a plain store_true action with default=False (so it has no --no- spelling), driven in the suite through the AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS env file. This is why the contract deliberately uses the different boolean/tri-state fixture --analytics.

Another unrelated default asserted by the contract: --check-update is BooleanOptionalAction with default=True and its env source is AIDER_CHECK_UPDATE (pinned to 'false' in the test setUp). An explicit --analytics/--no-analytics must not disturb it.

Sibling tri-state option (BooleanOptionalAction, default=None) consumed via main.py -> repo.py as coder.args.attribute_author; it shares the same contract shape as --analytics, confirming the tri-state default-None pattern is the repository's convention for options that must not be silently replaced by env/config input.

Documents how environment input reaches the parser: .env files are searched (cwd -> git root -> HOME, plus an explicit --env-file) and loaded with load_dotenv(..., override=True), so AIDER_* variables defined in env files land in os.environ and are then picked up by auto_env_var_prefix. This is the 'environment/config input' side of the precedence contract.

The decisive ordering: the parser is rebuilt with the resolved default_config_files (496), argv is pre-parsed (498), the .env files named by/around the args are loaded (501), and then the final args = parser.parse_args(argv) (504). Because the CLI vector is parsed last, explicit CLI input is applied after env-var/config-file defaults exist and therefore wins, while options absent from argv keep their declared defaults.

Consumption site of the tri-state fixture: need_to_ask returns False for exactly False, True for exactly True, and asserts args_analytics is None otherwise. That strict identity comparison proves the env/config strings must be coerced to real booleans (not left as truthy strings such as 'false'), which the contract's runtime matrix asserts for AIDER_ANALYTICS='false'.

The suite's baseline environment for the fixture: os.environ['AIDER_ANALYTICS'] = 'false' (plus AIDER_CHECK_UPDATE='false'), a throwaway HOME so no real ~/.aider.conf.yml leaks in, and tearDown restoring the original environment. Any test that reaches the analytics gate therefore proves AIDER_ANALYTICS is parsed into the tri-state value False rather than the truthy string 'false'.

The public acceptance pattern for 'explicit CLI input without changing unrelated defaults': main(['--no-auto-commits','--yes']) reaches Coder.create(auto_commits=False), main(['--auto-commits']) reaches auto_commits=True, the no-flag call main([]) still has dirty_commits=True and auto_commits=True, and main(['--no-dirty-commits']) flips only dirty_commits. Only the named option moves; the other defaulted options stay put.

Pins the non-CLI input layering the contract overrides: named --env-file beats cwd .env, which beats git-root .env, which beats HOME .env, and a variable already present in the process environment (E=existing) survives dotenv loading. So env/config values do reach the parser and are exactly what an explicit CLI token has to beat.

The already-fixtured boolean: .env containing AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=on makes Coder.create receive show_diffs=True. Its sibling test_false_vals_in_env_file (448-454) asserts AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=off yields show_diffs=False. Together they show env-string boolean coercion works for a two-state option — the different, tri-state option --analytics is what this contract adds.

Negative env-string case for the pre-existing fixture: AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=off must produce show_diffs=False (not a truthy string), i.e. env input for a boolean/optional option is normalized before it reaches the coder — the same normalization the contract asserts for AIDER_ANALYTICS=false.

Proves config-file input works and is ordered: .aider.conf.yml values in cwd (model=gpt-4-32k, map-tokens=4096), git root (gpt-4/2048) and HOME (gpt-3.5-turbo/1024) are picked up as the search path shrinks, and an explicit --config file (gpt-4-1106-preview/8192) wins. Since get_parser is re-parsed with argv last, a CLI token outranks these config values as well.

claims.claim: aider/args.py declares the boolean/tri-state fixture as --analytics with action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction and default=None, so it has three states (None = unset/ask, True = force on, False = force off) plus an explicit negative CLI spelling --no-analytics.

get_parser wires the two non-CLI input sources for that same key: environment variables through auto_env_var_prefix='AIDER_' (AIDER_ANALYTICS) and YAML config files through configargparse.YAMLConfigFileParser (the analytics: key of .aider.conf.yml).

aider.main.main resolves/rebuilds the parser from default_config_files, loads .env files (load_dotenv_files, override=True) and only then executes the final parser.parse_args(argv); explicit CLI tokens are therefore applied after env-var and config-file derived defaults, so CLI input wins while every option not named in argv keeps its declared default.

tests/basic/test_main.py::TestMain.test_main_args is the public acceptance pattern for 'explicit CLI input overrides input without changing unrelated defaults': the explicit boolean flags change exactly the named option (auto_commits/dirty_commits) while the no-flag call keeps dirty_commits=True and auto_commits=True, which matches the declared defaults of --auto-commits/--dirty-commits (and --git default=True) in aider/args.py.

The suite both pins the fixture's environment variable (AIDER_ANALYTICS='false' in TestMain.setUp) and requires env strings to be coerced to real booleans, because aider.analytics.Analytics.need_to_ask compares with 'is False'/'is True' and asserts args_analytics is None otherwise; a truthy string like 'false' would break every test that reaches the analytics gate.

The already-covered fixture is a different option: --show-diffs is a plain store_true/default=False option exercised through AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS env files, and env-file override ordering is pinned by test_env_file_override; hence this contract's tri-state fixture --analytics (AIDER_ANALYTICS / analytics: in .aider.conf.yml / --analytics|--no-analytics) is the new, non-duplicate case.

Because the fixture is tri-state (default None), proving override behaviour requires asserting the negative CLI spelling and the untouched unrelated defaults too: the demo's matrix covers defaults-only, env-only, config-only, env-over-config, --analytics over env+config with value false, and --no-analytics over env+config with value true, re-checking auto_commits/dirty_commits/git/gitignore/check_update/dry_run/attribute_author in every row.

conclusion: Contract established for the boolean/tri-state fixture --analytics (action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=None) in aider/args.py::get_parser. The contract is: (1) input precedence is explicit CLI token > AIDER_ANALYTICS environment variable > `analytics:` in .aider.conf.yml (or the default_config_files chain) > declared default None; (2) the explicit CLI spellings --analytics and --no-analytics override a conflicting env var and config-file value for the same option, including the tri-state None case and the negative spelling; (3) overriding only --analytics leaves unrelated defaults untouched (auto_commits=True, dirty_commits=True, git=True, gitignore=True, check_update=True, dry_run=False, attribute_author=None). The behaviour is guaranteed by the repository's own wiring (configargparse defaults from env/config plus the final parser.parse_args(argv) in aider/main.py::main) and mirrors the accepted pattern in tests/basic/test_main.py::TestMain.test_main_args. The executable demo .prale-eval/contract_demo.py encodes this contract as twelve stdlib AST/text checks (all passing here) plus a six-row runtime precedence matrix that must be executed in a dependency-complete environment; in this sandbox the runtime matrix is blocked because configargparse==1.7.5, shtab, litellm and GitPython are not installed and installing dependencies is out of scope. No repository source, task metadata, lock file or git configuration was modified.
